rows.evidence: Q1: Material and Method and Tables 2-7 - the authors collected lateral samples with emitters from 14 farms in Canakkale (1, 2 and 3 seasons of use) and tested them in a hydraulic laboratory at six pressures, reporting clogged-emitter rates, flow-pressure exponents and uniformity parameters (Cv, Us, Eu, Cu); they also report chemical analyses of seven irrigation water sources.
rows.notes: The study reports its own laboratory data on emitter clogging and uniformity loss in used drip laterals, attributing clogging to hardness/Ca-Mg precipitation and sediment under inadequate filtration and low operating pressure (40-70 kPa). It does not involve fertigation at all, and reports nothing on soil health effects (hypoxia, salt accumulation in the wetting front, nutrient supply, environmental contamination). The only overlap with the passage is 'dripper clogging', but the study links clogging to water quality rather than fertilizer injection, so it does not support the claim that fertigation causes these risks. The claim's function (soil_health) is not addressed.

notes: Full text appears complete. The study is a laboratory/field-sample survey of emitter clogging in drip systems in Canakkale, Turkey; no fertigation or soil measurements were made. Uncertainty measures (standard error of x exponent, Cv) exist for clogging/uniformity results but are irrelevant since Q2 is 'no'.
